Read the [Terminology](terminology.html) for the concepts used in this guide.


## About this guide

This guide splits a populated form into separate forms using the root records and their related data.

It also shows how to write typed R data into an empty form.

## Split a form

A form model declares fixed-cell metadata, table layouts, primary keys, and parent keys.
The caller supplies a structurally validated source workbook and an empty template for the same model version.

The bundled survey form model has a composite primary key `[station, observation_id]` on `Observations`.
Each output contains one observation and all fixed metadata, even when identifiers repeat across stations.

```{r split}
library(form.tools)
# Locate the installed example resources.
example_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", package = "form.model")
# Load the requested form model.
form_model_definition <- form.model::read_form_model(file.path(example_directory, "form.yaml"))
# Choose a temporary location for this example.
output_directory <- tempfile("survey-by-observation-")
# Split the input form into one output per root record.
split_manifest <- split_form_workbook(
  file.path(example_directory, "form.xlsx"), form_model_definition,
  root_sheet = "Observations",
  template = file.path(example_directory, "form-empty.xlsx"),
  directory = output_directory,
  shared_sheets = "Equipment"
)
# Display the output paths and their root record keys.
split_manifest
# Remove the temporary files created by this example.
unlink(output_directory, recursive = TRUE)
```

Output filenames retain the original basename and append the root primary-key values in model order.
For example, `form.xlsx` with key `[ST01, OBS-001]` produces `form_ST01_OBS-001.xlsx`.
Invalid filename characters become `_`; case-insensitive collisions and names exceeding 255 bytes are rejected.
The returned manifest maps each file to its source row and primary-key components.
Root key values are never interpreted as filesystem paths.

## Shared data

Fixed-cell model fields are copied into every output workbook.
Template sheets outside the model remain unchanged.
Source sheets outside the model are not copied.

The survey example copies the independent `Equipment` table with `shared_sheets = "Equipment"`.

All tables outside the selected hierarchy must be declared shared; the tool never silently drops such tables.

## Template requirements

The model and both workbooks must agree on worksheet names and physical layouts.
The caller selects the exact template version. Both workbooks must use the same Excel date system.

Table data regions must contain no values or formulas.
Prepare the first data row with the desired column styles and row height for additional records.
Existing styled rows are retained. Standard validation and conditional-formatting ranges are extended as needed.

Excel tables and merged cells in template data regions are not supported.
Fixed print areas and extended Excel validation ranges are preserved without expansion.

## Validation and publication

The source must already pass structural validation.
The splitter also checks required sheets, extents, complete and unique primary keys, and existing parent keys.
Other field and business-rule findings do not prevent splitting.

Source formulas contribute cached values only. Excel errors and formulas without caches in modeled fields are rejected.
Template formulas outside modeled fields are retained; the output requests recalculation when opened in Excel.
R does not recalculate formulas.

The output directory must be new, with an existing parent directory.
All output files are prepared before the directory is published; failures leave no partial output directory.
Neither the input workbook nor the template is modified.

## Write a form

Supply one data frame per modeled sheet, with a column for every field. Match sheet and field names exactly.

Column and sheet order may differ from the form model. Fixed-cell sheets need one row; tables may be empty.

```{r write}
# Locate the installed survey resources.
writer_example_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", package = "form.model")
# Load the form model that defines the destination cells and columns.
writer_form_model <- form.model::read_form_model(file.path(writer_example_directory, "form.yaml"))
# Prepare the single metadata record with a Date column.
writer_metadata <- data.frame(submission = "001", date = as.Date("2026-11-11"),
  contact_email = "survey@example.org", comment = "Example survey")
# Prepare one observation with numeric, logical and UTC date-time columns.
writer_observations <- data.frame(station = "ST01", count = 2L, length = 1.5, unit = "m",
  active = TRUE, observed_at = as.POSIXct("2026-11-11 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"),
  latitude = -12.5, longitude = 34, observation_id = "OBS-001", quality = 1L, observer = "ALICE")
# Supply the field columns even when there are no sample records.
writer_samples <- data.frame(station = character(), observation_id = character(), sample_no = integer(),
  minimum_length = numeric(), maximum_length = numeric(), unit = character())
# Supply an empty measurements table with its declared field types.
writer_measurements <- data.frame(station = character(), observation_id = character(),
  sample_no = integer(), reading_no = integer(), value = numeric())
# Supply an empty equipment table.
writer_equipment <- data.frame(equipment_id = character(), serial = character(), label = character())
# Supply an empty notes table.
writer_notes <- data.frame(station = character(), observation_id = character(), category = character(),
  count = integer(), confirmed = logical())
# Associate each data frame with its modeled sheet name.
writer_sheet_data <- list(Metadata = writer_metadata, Observations = writer_observations,
  Samples = writer_samples, Measurements = writer_measurements, Equipment = writer_equipment,
  Notes = writer_notes)
# Choose a new output path in an existing directory.
writer_output_path <- tempfile("survey-written-", fileext = ".xlsx")
# Populate the empty form without modifying the template.
write_form_workbook(writer_sheet_data, writer_form_model,
  template = file.path(writer_example_directory, "form-empty.xlsx"), path = writer_output_path)
# Remove the form created by this example.
unlink(writer_output_path)
```

Use character columns for text, logical columns for Booleans, `Date` for dates and `POSIXct` for date-times.

Numeric fields accept integer or numeric columns. Integer fields reject fractional values; missing values stay blank.

Text remains literal, including leading zeros and values starting with `=`. Input record order is preserved.

The writer uses the template's Excel date system and writes date-times in UTC.

Select the matching template version. Data regions must be empty; targeted formulas and merged cells are rejected.

Standard validation and conditional-formatting ranges expand with new rows; print areas remain unchanged.

Existing output files are never overwritten. Publication requires a filesystem supporting hard links.

The writer checks names, R types and writable positions. It does not check requiredness, keys or reference values.

Validate the populated form separately before treating it as a valid submission.

## Download the example files

```{r resource-links-1, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
# Use relative website links and installed resources in the package guide.
if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
  # Render links relative to the website article.
  cat("- [Form model \u2014 form.yaml](../examples/survey/form.yaml)\n- [Populated form \u2014 form.xlsx](../examples/survey/form.xlsx)\n- [Empty form \u2014 form-empty.xlsx](../examples/survey/form-empty.xlsx)\n")
} else {
  # Point readers to the installed package resources.
  cat("Find these files with `system.file(\"examples\", \"survey\", package = \"form.model\")`.\n")
}
```
